deals.source: This Week in CPG (May 5, 2026) via Axios

fundNews.details: Coefficient Capital closed Fund II at $290M and its Apex growth vehicle at $240M, bringing total new capital under management to $500M. The firm focuses on consumer and retail technology investments. The dual-close structure signals strong LP appetite for consumer-focused venture strategies at both the early and growth stages.

Manica Blain, founder of Top Knot Ventures, joined Consumer VC podcast (Episode #362) to discuss the state of early-stage consumer VC. The conversation explored whether the asset class is broken and what it takes to build durable consumer brands in the current market environment.

Collaborative Fund raised $250M for Collab Holdings, a new private equity vehicle focused on consumer brands. The fund represents a significant shift from their venture roots into later-stage growth equity and PE buyouts. Strong LP demand for consumer-focused PE strategies underscores the maturation of the consumer brand investment ecosystem.

L Catterton and Patricof Co announced the formation of CHAMP, a strategic partnership connecting top athletes with consumer investment opportunities. The platform allows athletes including Kevin Durant, Cooper Flagg, Livvy Dunne, and Cade Cunningham to co-invest alongside L Catterton in emerging and scaled consumer brands. CHAMP represents a novel convergence of celebrity/athlete capital and institutional consumer VC deal access.

True Beauty Ventures kicked off fundraising for Fund III. Since launching in 2020, the firm has backed brands including Vacation, K18, Jupiter, Crown Affair, and Biologica. The fund focuses on beauty, wellness, and personal care investments.

S2G Investments secured $1B for Solutions Fund I, focused on backing growth-stage startups in Europe and North America across food, agriculture, and energy. Previous S2G investments include 80 Acres Farms, Apeel Sciences, Atomo Coffee, and Bettani Farms. The fund's scale signals strong LP appetite for sustainable food systems investing at the growth stage.

Mother Ventures closed a $10M fund to support companies building healthy futures for mothers and their families. The fund reflects growing institutional interest in the maternal health and family wellness category, building on strong consumer demand for products and services supporting the perinatal journey.

e.l.f. Beauty transferred ownership of Keys Soulcare back to co-founder Alicia Keys as of May 21, 2026. The brand exit was announced during e.l.f.'s earnings call as the company refocuses on its five core growth brands including e.l.f. Cosmetics, rhode, Naturium, and W3LL People. Keys Soulcare was originally co-founded and incubated by e.l.f. in 2020.
fundNews.source: Thingtesting Newsletter / This Week in CPG

fundNews.details: Shein acquired San Francisco-based apparel brand Everlane for approximately $100 million. Everlane, known for its radical transparency positioning and minimalist staples, had been struggling with $90 million in debt. The brand will retain operational autonomy and its sustainability commitments under Shein ownership.

fundNews.fund: Heartland Food Products Group / Whole Earth Brands
fundNews.details: Heartland Food Products Group, the owner of Splenda, acquired the Americas business of Whole Earth Brands and its broad portfolio of natural sweeteners. Heartland now owns a diversified sweetener portfolio including Equal, Swerve, Whole Earth, Chuker, and Splenda. The deal consolidates two major players in the better-for-you sweetener category.

Scholl's Wellness Company, parent of the Dr. Scholl's brand, acquired performance-focused insole maker VKTRY. VKTRY is known for its carbon fiber insoles used by elite athletes to enhance performance and reduce injury risk. The acquisition expands Dr. Scholl's portfolio into the performance footwear innovation segment.

UK-based Imperial Brands (through ITG Brands) acquired tobacco alternative brand Black Buffalo for $150M plus earnout. Black Buffalo was founded in 2015 and backed by Listen Ventures, Vice Ventures, Access Capital, and Watchfire Ventures. The exit represents a notable consumer CPG M&A outcome for early-stage backers in the smokeless tobacco alternatives space.

Global dairy giant Lactalis acquired UK-based sports nutrition brand Protein Works for an undisclosed sum. Protein Works, founded in 2012 in Liverpool, generates ~$75M in annual sales across protein supplements and nutrition products. The deal follows Danone's $1.15B acquisition of Huel earlier in 2026, signaling accelerating Big Food/Dairy consolidation into functional nutrition.

fundNews.fund: Church & Dwight / Miss Mouth's Messy Eater
fundNews.details: Church & Dwight (NYSE: CHD) acquired Miss Mouth's Messy Eater for $325M. Thrasio had purchased the brand in 2020 and scaled it into the largest stain remover brand on Amazon, generating $80M net sales and $28M EBITDA in 2025. The acquisition continues Church & Dwight's disciplined acquisition playbook and highlights how Amazon-native brands can achieve significant strategic exits.

Animal Capital closed Fund III with $33 million in total commitments on June 10, 2026. Led by founder Marshall Sandman, the fund nearly doubles the firm's prior vehicle and targets early-stage, primarily U.S.-based consumer tech investments that leverage technology to improve consumer lives. Fund III increases the firm's target check size by approximately 150% versus its inaugural fund.

points.label: Garner Health's $100M Series E at $2.74B Validates Consumer Healthcare Navigation at Scale
points.context: Index Ventures led Garner Health's $100M Series E at a $2.74B valuation, making it one of the largest consumer health tech rounds of the year. Garner helps employers steer employees toward higher-quality, lower-cost doctors — a model that sits at the confluence of employer benefits, consumer behavior change, and healthcare cost reduction. The scale of this round, led by a generalist tier-1 fund, signals that consumer healthcare navigation has crossed from 'interesting niche' to 'category-defining infrastructure.'
points.take: Garner's $2.74B valuation anchors the consumer health navigation category as institutional — founders building adjacent services (mental health navigation, specialty care routing, diagnostic guidance) now have a credible comparables framework for Series A and B conversations, and should lean into the 'cost reduction + quality improvement' narrative rather than pure 'consumer wellness' positioning when pitching institutional funds.

points.label: Airbnb Leads WeRoad's $58M Series C — Strategic Investors Are Taking the Lead Investor Seat
points.context: Airbnb led WeRoad's $58M Series C for the European group travel marketplace — a notable instance of a major platform company taking the lead investor seat in a consumer marketplace round rather than a financial VC. WeRoad specializes in community-driven group travel for solo travelers, a segment that aligns with Airbnb's own community-first positioning. The deal reflects a broader pattern in 2026 of strategic corporates writing lead checks in adjacent consumer categories rather than deferring to financial sponsors.
points.take: Strategic-led rounds like WeRoad's signal a structural shift in late-stage consumer marketplace funding dynamics — founders in travel, social, or community-commerce categories should treat platform companies (Airbnb, Duolingo, Reddit) as viable Series B/C lead candidates rather than just distribution partners, especially where the strategic value of the relationship is more defensible than what any financial VC could provide.

points.label: L Catterton's REMEDY Series A Reinforces PE's Continued Appetite for Early-Stage Consumer Health
points.context: L Catterton led REMEDY's $20M Series A alongside Norwest and Sonoma Brands Capital — a significant signal given that L Catterton typically deploys growth equity at later stages. The deal follows L Catterton's participation in the California Naturals Series B last week, suggesting the fund is deliberately moving earlier in the consumer health and wellness category. REMEDY's personal care positioning in the health-beauty convergence space continues to attract premium lead investors.
points.take: L Catterton writing two consecutive A/B-stage checks in a single week is a meaningful deployment signal — consumer health founders in the $10-25M Series A range should treat L Catterton as an active target for lead conversations rather than assuming they'll wait for growth stage, particularly if the brand is positioned at the intersection of health outcomes and premium consumer aesthetics.

points.label: Food & Bev M&A Continues at Pace: Two Exits in One Week
points.context: Second Nature Brands acquired Tillamook Country Smoker and an undisclosed buyer acquired Wize Tea — two CPG food exits in the same week from Consumer VC Roundup #156. These add to a Q2 2026 pattern of sustained M&A activity in food & bev where strategic acquirers and holding companies are actively scooping up established brands at various stages. The clustering of exits in the June timeframe suggests acquirers are deploying capital before summer slowdown windows.
points.take: The continued Food & Bev exit cadence in Q2 2026 is a positive signal for seed and Series A CPG founders — acquirers are clearly active and the pipeline of strategic buyers in food has diversified beyond the traditional Big Food players to include brand holding companies and PE-backed platforms, suggesting multiple potential exit channels rather than a single buyer-of-last-resort dynamic.

points.label: Hardware Emerges as an Overlooked Seed Opportunity: Kalogon + Sychedelic Both Raise at Seed
points.context: Two hardware-focused consumer tech companies raised seed rounds this week: Kalogon ($5.75M, smart wheelchair cushion technology) and Sychedelic ($3.5M, consumer brain stimulation wearables). Both tackle deeply physical problems — mobility and cognitive enhancement — that software-only approaches cannot solve. Hardware consumer deals remain a small fraction of overall consumer VC volume despite the category's potential for defensibility through physical product moats.
points.take: Hardware-native consumer companies at the seed stage are often systematically underpriced by software-trained VCs who underestimate defensibility at the intersection of physical form factor and health outcomes — the Kalogon and Sychedelic raises, both at the seed stage, suggest that specialized investors are finding asymmetric opportunities in categories that generalist software funds routinely pass on.

points.label: European Supplement Brands Attracting Cross-Border Institutional Capital
points.context: Rem3dy Health (Nourished), a UK-based personalized nutrition brand, raised £14M (~$18.8M) in a Series A, while French supplement company Laboratoire Nutergia was acquired by 3i Group (Growth) in the same week. Together, these deals reflect growing institutional appetite for European supplement and functional nutrition brands — a category that has historically been concentrated in the US and Australian markets. The 3i deal in particular signals PE-level conviction in European supplement scale.
points.take: The simultaneous institutional investment and PE acquisition of European supplement brands signals that the category is approaching a professionalization inflection point in Europe — US-focused supplement investors should be developing European deal flow now before category multiples compress as PE platforms consolidate the most attractive assets.

points.label: Animal Capital's $33M Fund III Shows Micro-VC Consumer Tech Is Institutionalizing
points.context: Animal Capital closed Fund III at $33M — nearly double the prior vehicle — with lead Marshall Sandman targeting early-stage US consumer tech companies that use technology to improve consumer lives. The fund's growth in size and LP base mirrors a broader trend of specialist consumer tech micro-funds achieving institutional maturity after initial vintage performance. Animal Capital increases its check size by approximately 150% vs. its inaugural fund, enabling it to compete more aggressively for conviction A-round opportunities.
points.take: The institutionalization of micro-fund consumer VC — with Animal Capital III now writing meaningfully larger checks — is compressing the gap between seed-stage specialists and traditional A-round institutional VCs, creating a new competitive dynamic where founders in the pre-Series A window have more qualified lead options than at any prior point in the consumer VC cycle.
